info.title: unilyze - Static analyzer for Unity projects
info.description: CLI tool to analyze Unity project .asmdef and C# source code with Roslyn, generating dependency graphs and code quality metrics.

options.name: --metric
options.description: Badge metric: codehealth, mi, smells (default: codehealth)

options.name: --level
options.description: Pin analysis level: syntax, core, full, complete

options.name: --fail-under
options.description:
Quality gate for codehealth/mi: fail if value below threshold
(codehealth: min CodeHealth, mi: average MI)

options.name: --fail-over
options.description:
Quality gate for smells: fail if warning count above count
(any critical smell always fails)

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
Exit codes:
0  Success / gate passed
1  Usage error (e.g. --fail-under with --metric smells)
2  Quality gate failed
Output format (shields.io endpoint JSON or flat SVG):
{ "schemaVersion": 1, "label": "...", "message": "...", "color": "...", "analysisLevel": "..." }
shields.io ignores the extra analysisLevel field.
SVG: single-line shields.io flat badge (use --format svg);
the analysis level is embedded as a leading XML comment.

commands.name: statusline
commands.description: Output compact code health for status line display

options.name: --level
options.description: Pin analysis level: syntax, core, full, complete

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
Output format: CH:9.4 ⚠87 🔴5 [core]
CH       = Average Code Health (1.0-10.0)
⚠        = Warning code smells count
🔴       = Critical code smells count (hidden if 0)
[level]  = Analysis level marker, shown only below Complete
([syntax] / [core] / [full])
Color coding:
Code Health: green (>=8.0), yellow (>=5.0), red (<5.0)
Warnings: yellow
Criticals: red
Cache:
Results are cached in /tmp/unilyze-sl-{hash}.txt
Use --refresh to control cache lifetime (default: 60 seconds)

options.name: --path
options.description: Unity project root or Assets directory (default: .)

options.name: --input
options.description: Use existing JSON instead of analyzing

options.name: --output
options.description: Output file path (format inferred from extension: .html, .json, .sarif)

options.name: --format
options.description: Output format: html, json, sarif (default: html)

options.name: --assembly
options.description: Filter by assembly name (exact or suffix match, e.g. "Domain" matches "App.Domain")

options.name: --prefix
options.description: Filter asmdef names by prefix (auto-detected from common dot-prefix if omitted)

options.name: --exclude-dir
options.description: Exclude directory from analysis (repeatable, relative to project root)

options.name: --level
options.description:
Pin analysis level: syntax, core, full, complete
(caps auto-resolved level; fails if the level cannot be reached)

options.name: --no-open
options.description: Do not open the generated HTML in a browser

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help
Configuration:
Settings are loaded from (all scopes merged additively):
Global:  $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/unilyze/config.json (default: ~/.config/unilyze/config.json)
Project: <project-root>/.unilyze.json
Example .unilyze.json:
{ "excludeDirs": ["Assets/Plugins", "Assets/ThirdParty"] }
